summary: RFC 9252 defines BGP overlay services for SRv6. This RFC updates it with more detailed specifications for signaling and processing of SRv6 Segment Identifiers that have arguments.

eli5.summary: Some network addresses carry extra info. This clarifies how that info is sent and read.

questions: what is srv6 sid argument length
what is esi filtering in evpn
subtitle: Clarifies how BGP advertises SRv6 segment IDs that carry an argument, and how the receiver rebuilds them.

tldr.problem: RFC 9252 explained how to signal SRv6 service SIDs with arguments for EVPN, but implementation and interoperability testing found it too vague. Its bitwise-OR rule also assumed every advertised SID has the same structure.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC spells out what the Ethernet A-D per ES route and the Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag route must carry, including the Argument Length (AL), and gives the ingress PE a step-by-step procedure to combine them.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 9252. SIDs can now have different structures in the two route types, and an AL mismatch is treated as a configuration error that stops BUM forwarding for that Ethernet Segment.

today: RFC 9819 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2025 that updates RFC 9252. It has not been obsoleted or updated itself.

sections.title: Why RFC 9252 Needed a Fix
sections.content:
In SRv6, a Segment Identifier (SID) tied to a service-specific behavior on a Provider Edge (PE) router is called an SRv6 Service SID. RFC 9252 defines how BGP signals such services for L3VPN, EVPN and Internet routing. For some EVPN services, RFC 8986 introduced the End.DT2M behavior, which uses an argument (Arg.FE2).

During implementation and interoperability testing, RFC 9252 turned out to lack detail, which led to ambiguous readings. This document adds the missing detail. It focuses on End.DT2M, but the procedures also apply to other similar behaviors with arguments signaled in BGP.

It also removes a restriction. RFC 9252 derives the data-plane SID by a bitwise OR of the SID from the Ethernet A-D per ES route and the SID from the Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag route. That assumes both use the same SID structure, which is not universally valid. The examples do not use the Transposition Scheme, and the RFC does not change how it is used.
sections.eli5: The first set of rules left room for two people to read them differently, so their routers did not agree. This one fills in the gaps.

sections.title: SIDs, Arguments and Argument Length
sections.content:
An SRv6 SID has up to three parts: Locator (LOC), Function (FUNC) and Argument (ARG). If a behavior takes no argument, all bits after FUNC MUST be zero and the Argument Length (AL) MUST be zero.

When a behavior such as End.DT2M supports arguments, the SRv6 SID Structure Sub-Sub-TLV MUST be included. A zero AL means the node accepts no argument for that SID. A non-zero AL gives the argument size, and together with the Locator Block Length (LBL), Locator Node Length (LNL) and Function Length (FL) it tells where the ARG sits. All bits beyond LBL + LNL + FL + AL MUST be zero.

The LOC:FUNC part and the ARG may be advertised separately, by the SID owner or by another node or mechanism. Whoever advertises an ARG MUST give its size, its value and the SID's behavior, and MUST say which SIDs it applies to. The SRv6 source node then appends the ARG to build the full LOC:FUNC:ARG SID, used as an IPv6 destination address or as a segment in the Segment Routing Header.
sections.eli5: A SID is like an address with a street, a house and sometimes a room number. The length field tells everyone how many digits the room number has, and zero means there is no room number.

sections.title: What Each EVPN Route Advertises
sections.content:
For End.DT2M, the LOC:FUNC part goes in the Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag route, and the ESI Filtering argument goes in the Ethernet A-D per ES route. ESI Filtering is a split-horizon mechanism, used with multihoming or E-Tree, that stops the disposition PE forwarding broadcast, unknown unicast and multicast (BUM) traffic to local Ethernet Segments or leaf circuits.

Ethernet A-D per ES route. Without ESI Filtering, the route SHOULD still carry an SRv6 L2 Service TLV with the SID set to ::0 and behavior End.DT2M, with a SID Structure Sub-Sub-TLV and AL of 0. With ESI Filtering, it MUST carry the SID containing the ARG, AL set to the argument size (which SHOULD be a multiple of 8), and LBL, LNL and FL set to show the ARG offset. LBL, LNL and FL MUST follow the real structure of End.DT2M SIDs, not be set to 0, to stay compatible with RFC 9252.

Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag route. It MUST carry only the LOC:FUNC part, with a structure sub-sub-TLV. AL is 0 without ESI Filtering. With it, AL MUST be the supported argument size, and the egress PE MUST use the same AL for all local Ethernet Segments in the same broadcast domain. The AL here MUST equal the AL in the matching Ethernet A-D per ES route.
sections.eli5: One note carries the main address and another carries the room number. Both notes must agree on how long the room number is.

sections.title: How the Ingress PE Builds the SID
sections.content:
The ingress PE learns the LOC:FUNC part from the Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag route and the ARG from the Ethernet A-D per ES route, then follows these steps.

  1. If AL is 0 in the Inclusive Multicast route, the SID is the LOC:FUNC part only, with all bits after LBL + LNL + FL set to zero. The router MUST ignore the SID and structure in the Ethernet A-D per ES route.
  2. If AL is non-zero there, the router finds the matching Ethernet A-D per ES route and checks for an End.DT2M SID.
    • If none is found, or its AL is zero, no usable ARG exists and the SID is formed as in step 1.
    • If both ALs are non-zero but unequal, that is a configuration error. To prevent looping, BUM traffic MUST NOT be forwarded for those routes from that Ethernet Segment, and implementations SHOULD log an error.
    • If both are non-zero and equal, the ARG is encoded into the LOC:FUNC SID at offset LBL + LNL + FL, with all bits beyond LBL + LNL + FL + AL set to zero.

If the PE expects ESI Filtering but gets no usable ARG, it SHOULD log a message.

In the RFC's Figure 6, LOC:FUNC 2001:db8:1:fbd1:: and ARG ::aaaa:0:0:0, both with LBL 32, LNL 16, FL 16 and AL 16, give the data-plane SID 2001:db8:1:fbd1:aaaa::.
sections.eli5: The receiver checks that both notes agree on the room number length. If they do, it writes the room number onto the address. If they disagree, it stops sending the risky party invitations to avoid a loop.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility
sections.content:
Implementations that use the bitwise OR from Section 6.3 of RFC 9252 work correctly only when the SID structures of the two EVPN route types are identical. Compatibility is kept when the Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag route and its Ethernet A-D per ES route advertise the same structure, as Sections 3.1 and 3.2 require.

When the structures differ, the OR cannot be used, and the method in the ingress PE procedure MUST be used instead. This is why the RFC insists that LBL, LNL and FL reflect the real SID structure instead of being zeroed.
sections.eli5: The old way of gluing the notes together still works when both notes look alike. When they differ, use the new, more careful way.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The document gives a more detailed specification of the signaling and processing of SRv6 SID advertisements for behaviors with arguments. It states that it introduces no new security considerations beyond those already covered in RFC 9252. It has no IANA actions.
sections.eli5: This only makes the existing rules clearer, so it adds no new safety worries and needs no new registry entries.
